body_markdown:
Building AI chatbots no longer requires a dedicated development team, months of work, or complex infrastructure setup. Platforms like[Floot](https://floot.com/) let non-technical founders create chatbot-enabled applications with managed databases, authentication, and hosting. The[low-code platform market](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/low-code-development-platform-market-102972) was valued at $37.39 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach $376.92 billion by 2034, reflecting growing demand for accessible app development.


For chatbot builders, choosing the right platform matters. A 2026 Gartner survey found customers were approximately[three times more likely](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-07-08-gartner-survey-finds-customers-are-three-times-more-likely-to-use-third-party-genai-than-company-provided-chatbots-for-customer-service) to use third-party GenAI tools than company-provided chatbots for customer service. Meanwhile,[83% of respondents](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/ai/data/ai-select) to Stack Overflow's 2026 Developer Survey reported using at least one AI tool at work. The 13 platforms below offer different approaches to building, connecting, and deploying chatbots.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Accessible full-stack development:** Floot provides managed PostgreSQL, authentication, storage, and hosting, helping non-technical founders build chatbot applications without configuring separate infrastructure.
- **No separate AI build-credit charges:** Teams already paying for Claude or ChatGPT can[build through their assistant](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) using Floot's MCP connector without separate AI credits for standard connector-based building.
- **Mobile deployment options:** Floot supports iOS and Android app packaging without requiring a Mac or Xcode. Mobile-build allowances depend on the plan, and store publishing requires developer accounts and approval.
- **Code ownership and portability:** Floot users own their project code, data, and intellectual property, with database export available on every plan and downloadable project code on paid plans.
- **Managed infrastructure:** Floot is suited to teams prioritizing saved data, user accounts,[mobile deployment](https://floot.com/en/mobile) , and integrations with existing AI assistants.


## **What to Look For in an AI App Builder for Chatbots**


Building a chatbot app involves more than generating conversational interfaces. A production-ready chatbot needs backend infrastructure, user authentication, data persistence, and reliable hosting. The AI app builder chosen should address these requirements without forcing management of separate services.


When evaluating platforms for chatbot development, consider:


- **AI assistant integration:** Can building happen using Claude, ChatGPT, or other AI tools already subscribed to?
- **Backend infrastructure:** Does the platform include managed databases, authentication, and file storage?
- **Mobile deployment:** Can the chatbot be packaged as an installable iOS or Android app?
- **Code ownership:** Can code and data be exported if migration is needed?
- **Pricing model:** Are charges based on AI credits, build actions, or hosting usage?
- **Security and compliance:** Does the platform support enterprise requirements like SSO and audit trails?


The platforms below represent different approaches to these requirements. Some prioritize speed over customization. Others offer full developer control with additional technical complexity.


## **1. Floot**


Floot is a full-stack app-building platform with an[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Floot provides managed infrastructure while the connected AI assistant handles development, with available building capabilities depending on the client's connector permissions.


### **Why It Fits Chatbot Development**


Floot's primary differentiator is its BYOM (Bring Your Own Model) approach. For standard connector-based building, Floot lets users work through their existing Claude or ChatGPT subscription without separate Floot AI build-credit charges. Image generation and AI features running inside published apps are exceptions. The platform meters connector work through build actions rather than charging for the connected assistant's model usage.


For chatbot apps specifically, Floot provides the backend infrastructure that conversational applications require: managed PostgreSQL databases, user authentication with Google and Microsoft OAuth, file storage, email notifications, and real-time capabilities. Live chatbot responses can use Floot AI credits or a separately billed external model provider. Applications can be built by[describing requirements](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) in natural language through a connected AI assistant.


### **Chatbot-Relevant Capabilities**


- MCP connector for Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations
- Managed PostgreSQL, authentication, storage, and email included with every project
- Real-time updates and serverless backend logic for conversational applications
- [Mobile app packaging](https://floot.com/en/mobile) for iOS and Android without requiring a Mac or Xcode
- Optional server-side pre-rendering for crawlable public pages
- TypeScript and React codebase, with code ownership on every plan and project ZIP downloads on paid plans
- Support for connecting external AI providers and business services


### **How Floot Makes Building and Publishing Easier**


Floot is free to start and provides an integrated environment for building, testing, and publishing applications. Its[built-in services](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) reduce the need to configure separate database, authentication, hosting, and storage providers. Users can also[connect custom domains](https://floot.com/docs/custom-domains/how-to-add-custom-domain) on paid plans and manage application updates through supported AI assistants.


According to Floot's[current pricing](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , checked November 8, 2026:


- **Free ($0/month):** 100 build actions per day, 3,000 one-time starter AI credits, a one-time $3 hosting credit, and 2 mobile builds per month.
- **Pro ($25/month):** 1,000 daily build actions, 5,000 monthly AI credits, a $10 monthly hosting allowance, 12 mobile builds per month, and custom domains.
- **Power ($100/month):** 5,000 daily build actions, 15,000 monthly AI credits, a $25 monthly hosting allowance, and unlimited mobile builds.


Annual billing provides two months free on paid plans. Hosting beyond the included allowance draws on prepaid hosting credit, with optional auto-reload. Existing AI subscriptions are billed separately from Floot, while downloadable project ZIP exports are available on paid plans.


## **2. Lovable**


Lovable is a prompt-driven web app builder that generates full-stack applications from natural language descriptions. The platform[surpassed $500 million](https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/09/lovable-says-it-has-hit-500m-in-annualized-revenue-with-1-million-new-projects-a-week/) in annualized revenue by June 2026.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Rapid prototyping:** Prompt-driven generation for quick chatbot interface creation
- **Full-stack generation:** Frontend, backend, and database functionality from natural language
- **Autonomous building:** Agent Mode for complex, multi-step development changes


### **Key Features**


- Full-stack generation from prompts, including frontend and backend functionality
- GitHub integration for code export and continued development
- Agent Mode for handling complex, multi-step changes autonomously
- Managed backend capabilities and Supabase integration options


### **Organizational Fit**


Lovable uses a credit-based pricing model with its own AI for generation. Teams should compare whether credit-based or BYOM pricing better fits their usage patterns. The platform focuses primarily on web applications rather than native mobile development.


## **3. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new is a browser-based development platform from StackBlitz that emphasizes speed from prompt to deployed app.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Browser-based development:** Zero-setup environment running entirely in the browser
- **Iterative development:** Supports chatbot interfaces and logic through a conversational development environment
- **Mobile support:** Expo support for React Native mobile apps


### **Key Features**


- Zero-setup development environment running entirely in the browser
- Bolt Cloud backend with database, authentication, and hosting
- GitHub sync and ZIP download for code export
- Expo support for mobile app generation
- Free tier with 1 million tokens per month and a 300,000-token daily limit


### **Organizational Fit**


Bolt.new offers a browser-based path from prompt to deployed app. Teams should evaluate whether its token-based pricing model aligns with expected development usage, particularly as projects become more complex.


## **4. Lindy**


Lindy is an AI teammate platform that includes Lindy Build for creating full-stack applications with built-in QA testing.


### **Primary Focus**


- **AI teammate integration:** Platform works in Slack and connects with existing business tools
- **Built-in testing:** Creates apps and tests them automatically rather than delivering untested code
- **Enterprise connectivity:** More than 1,500 integrations for connecting chatbot workflows to business systems


### **Key Features**


- Built-in QA testing that behaves like a human tester
- More than 1,500 integrations for connecting to business systems
- SOC 2 compliance, with HIPAA support and signed BAA availability on Enterprise
- Conversational building with natural language refinement
- MCP support for extended capabilities


### **Organizational Fit**


Lindy is relevant for teams building internal chatbots that need to connect with existing business systems. The platform offers a free trial with $50 in credits, valid for seven days. Team plans start at $29.99 per active user per month, with a shared credit pool.


## **5. Replit Agent**


Replit Agent is an autonomous AI development platform that builds, tests, and fixes applications with minimal supervision.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Autonomous development:** Generates code, runs it, tests it, fixes errors, and deploys applications
- **Self-checking loops:** Identifies and attempts to resolve errors automatically
- **iOS deployment:** Launch tooling for preparing and uploading builds to App Store Connect


### **Key Features**


- Autonomous building, testing, and fixing cycle
- Built-in PostgreSQL database and authentication
- iOS deployment workflows involving App Store Connect
- Full browser-based IDE with terminal access
- Self-checking development loops


### **Organizational Fit**


Replit's autonomous approach suits teams that want to describe requirements and let AI handle implementation details. Pricing includes a free Starter tier, Core at $20 per month, and Pro at $100 per month. Annual billing reduces Core to $18 per month and Pro to $90 per month.


## **6. Bubble**


Bubble is an established no-code platform with over 12 years of development and a large plugin ecosystem.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Visual workflow engine:** Handles detailed business logic through a visual interface
- **Complex applications:** Supports multi-step decision trees, user role management, and custom business rules
- **Mature ecosystem:** Large plugin marketplace for extending functionality


### **Key Features**


- Visual workflow engine for complex business logic
- Large plugin ecosystem for extending functionality
- Native iOS and Android app-building capabilities
- Web and mobile apps sharing one backend
- AI features integrated into the visual builder


### **Organizational Fit**


Bubble has a steeper learning curve than prompt-based builders but offers control over complex applications. Source-code export is not available, which may matter for teams requiring code portability. Web Starter plans begin at $32 per month when billed annually, while Mobile Starter begins at $42 per month and combined Web and Mobile Starter at $59 per month, both billed annually.


## **7. FlutterFlow**


FlutterFlow is a visual Flutter app builder that generates exportable, cross-platform code.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Cross-platform native apps:** Exportable Flutter code for iOS, Android, web, and desktop
- **Streamlined deployment:** Supports deployment workflows for both the App Store and Google Play
- **Code ownership:** Generates Flutter and Dart code developers can continue working with


### **Key Features**


- Exportable Flutter code for iOS, Android, web, and desktop
- Streamlined deployment workflows for App Store and Google Play
- Visual builder with AI assistance
- Cross-platform development from a single codebase
- Professional framework based on Google's Flutter


### **Organizational Fit**


FlutterFlow is the visual builder described here. It connects to services such as Firebase and Supabase and supports Flutter source-code downloads on paid plans. The separate AI-native FlutterFlow experience includes a built-in backend but does not currently support source-code export. Studio's Free plan supports up to 2 projects; paid plans start at $39 per month for Basic and $80 per month for Pro.


## **8. Cursor**


Cursor is an AI-powered code editor that can work alongside Floot's MCP connector for managed application infrastructure. The platform was[acquired by SpaceX](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026056945/spcx-20260814.htm) in August 2026.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Developer-focused tool:** AI-powered code editor for developers wanting direct control
- **Multi-file AI agents:** Works across multiple files using project context
- **Framework flexibility:** Supports development across different languages, frameworks, and stacks


### **Key Features**


- Multi-file AI agents that edit across entire projects
- Built on VS Code with deep codebase understanding
- Support for multiple languages and frameworks
- Code remaining within developer-controlled repositories
- Multiple AI model options, subject to plan availability


### **Organizational Fit**


Cursor is a developer tool rather than a standalone no-code platform. Technical teams can pair Cursor with[Floot's MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) for managed hosting, PostgreSQL, authentication, and other backend services. Cursor pricing includes Free, Plus at $8 per month, and Premium at $30 per month. Plus provides Grok model access, while eligible third-party models on Premium are billed separately based on usage.


## **9. v0 by Vercel**


v0 is Vercel's AI app builder for full-stack applications, with Next.js as its default framework.


### **Primary Focus**


- **React and Next.js focus:** Generates React components using TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/ui
- **Vercel ecosystem integration:** Deployment workflows and marketplace integration
- **Design and code workflow:** Design Mode for visual editing alongside AI generation


### **Key Features**


- React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS output
- Vercel deployment integration
- GitHub sync for version control
- Design Mode for visual editing alongside AI generation
- Integration with the Vercel marketplace for backend services


### **Organizational Fit**


v0 supports full-stack application development as well as UI generation. Teams should evaluate the database, authentication, and hosting integrations their chatbot requires. Pricing is credit-based, with a Free plan offering $5 in one-time credits for new users and a Plus plan starting at $30 per user per month.


## **10. Base44**


Base44 is a full-stack AI app builder that was[acquired by Wix](https://techcrunch.com/2025/06/18/6-month-old-solo-owned-vibe-coder-base44-sells-to-wix-for-80m-cash/) for approximately $80 million in June 2025.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Managed infrastructure:** Built-in authentication, database, and storage
- **Application generation:** AI-generated frontend and backend from natural-language prompts
- **Entry-level pricing:** Starter plan available with annual billing


### **Key Features**


- AI-generated frontend and backend from natural-language prompts
- Built-in authentication, database, and storage
- iOS and Android store-file generation on Builder plans or higher, with separate developer accounts and submission required
- Credit-based AI application generation
- All-in-one stack without separate backend management


### **Organizational Fit**


Base44 generates applications with built-in database and authentication capabilities. For chatbot applications requiring specific data models, teams should review the generated backend against their requirements. For mobile publishing, Base44 can generate iOS and Android store files on Builder or higher plans, while users handle submission through their own developer accounts. The platform offers Starter at $16 per month and Builder at $40 per month, both billed annually.


## **11. Retool**


Retool is an internal tools platform with AI capabilities for building secure, data-connected applications.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Internal tools focus:** Designed for building internal chatbots and admin tools
- **Enterprise security:** Role-based controls and audit logs on higher-tier plans, with SSO available on Enterprise
- **Data connectivity:** Native integrations with databases and business systems


### **Key Features**


- AI-powered app builder generally available since October 28, 2026
- Role-based controls and audit logs on Business and Enterprise plans
- Native integrations with databases and business systems
- Retool Agents for automating work across company systems
- iOS, Android, and PWA deployment options


### **Organizational Fit**


Retool is designed primarily for internal tools rather than general-purpose customer-facing applications. The free tier supports up to 5 users, with Team plans starting at $10 per builder per month when billed annually, plus $5 per internal user per month on that plan.


## **12. AI by Zapier**


AI by Zapier brings AI reasoning and tool calling into Zap workflows connected to more than 9,000 app integrations. It replaced the standalone Zapier Agents workflow in October 2026.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Automation-focused:** AI-powered steps for lead qualification and business workflows
- **Integration breadth:** Connects AI workflows to more than 9,000 app integrations
- **Template library:** Templates for common automation patterns


### **Key Features**


- AI-powered reasoning and tool calls within Zap workflows
- Templates for common automation patterns
- Workflows that run on command or through configured triggers
- Task-based usage through Zapier's automation plans
- Connection to Zapier's broader automation ecosystem


### **Organizational Fit**


AI by Zapier is more automation-focused than app-building. It suits teams that need chatbot workflows connecting multiple existing services rather than building standalone chatbot applications. Its usage follows Zapier's task-based billing rather than the former standalone Agents activity-based plans.


## **13. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites lets eligible users build, preview, publish, and share interactive websites and applications through ChatGPT.


### **Primary Focus**


- **ChatGPT-native building:** Natural-language website and application creation inside ChatGPT
- **Interactive experiences:** Suited to dashboards, conversational interfaces, portals, and interactive resources
- **Quick sharing:** Interactive interfaces with preview and publishing workflows


### **Key Features**


- Natural-language website and application creation inside ChatGPT
- Interactive interfaces with preview and publishing workflows
- Support for connected apps using visitors' authorized permissions
- D1 relational database and R2 file-storage capabilities within supported limits
- Sharing and access controls for published sites


### **Organizational Fit**


ChatGPT Sites supports hosted web applications with database and storage capabilities, while Floot provides a managed full-stack environment with PostgreSQL, application authentication, hosting, and iOS and Android publishing workflows.


Teams building customer-facing chatbot products should compare their requirements for backend architecture, account management, external integrations, and mobile distribution. ChatGPT Sites is available on eligible paid ChatGPT plans, with building usage and hosting subject to plan-specific limits.


## **Why Floot Stands Out for AI Chatbot Building**


Chatbot development requires more than a conversational interface. Applications often need persistent conversation history, secure user accounts, backend logic, and reliable hosting.[Floot](https://floot.com/) provides these capabilities through managed infrastructure, while supported AI assistants handle development through its MCP connector. This makes it particularly relevant for non-technical founders building functional chatbot products.


Floot offers several capabilities for chatbot development:


- **Existing AI subscriptions:** Build through Claude or compatible ChatGPT configurations without separate Floot AI credits for standard connector work.
- **Managed backend:** PostgreSQL, authentication, file storage, email, and hosting through[built-in services](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) .
- **Mobile deployment:** Create iOS and Android builds without a Mac, subject to plan allowances, developer accounts, and store approval.
- **Code ownership:** Own project code, data, and IP, with database export on every plan and ZIP downloads on paid plans.
- **Flexible integrations:** Connect external AI providers and other business services while keeping application infrastructure managed.


For founders and operators, Floot connects AI-assisted development with the infrastructure needed to run a working chatbot application. Its[MCP integration](https://floot.com/blog/what-is-mcp-a-simple-guide-to-model-context-protocol-for-ai-apps) also lets builders work within familiar AI tools, subject to each client's connector permissions.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **Can a production chatbot be built with a free AI app builder tier?**


Yes, but free tiers usually have limits on building actions, hosting, AI usage, or deployment. Floot is free to start, with 100 build actions per day, 3,000 one-time starter AI credits, a one-time $3 hosting credit, and 2 mobile builds per month. These allowances can support early development and testing. For production chatbots with consistent traffic, teams should assess expected hosting usage, AI inference costs, database requirements, and ongoing maintenance. Floot's paid plans include monthly hosting allowances and higher daily building-action limits. Hosting beyond the included allowance draws on prepaid credit, so operating costs depend partly on actual application usage.


### **Is coding experience needed to build a chatbot with these platforms?**


Most AI app builders on this list support non-technical users through conversational interfaces. Platforms like Floot, Lovable, and Bolt.new allow users to describe requirements in natural language instead of manually implementing every feature. Cursor is primarily designed for developers who want AI-assisted coding and direct control over their projects. With Floot, supported AI assistants can create, edit, test, and publish applications through the MCP connector while Floot provides the backend infrastructure. The available actions depend on the assistant's connector permissions. Although coding experience is not required to start, reviewing chatbot responses, testing user authentication, checking data handling, and validating integrations remain important before production use.


### **How to choose between BYOM and credit-based pricing models?**


BYOM (Bring Your Own Model) platforms like Floot allow users to build with existing AI subscriptions, which may reduce additional AI build-credit charges when Claude or ChatGPT is already part of their workflow. Floot meters standard connector work through building actions rather than charging separately for the connected assistant's model usage. Credit-based platforms include AI usage within their own pricing structures, often with limits that depend on the complexity of generated work. When comparing costs, account for the existing AI subscription, Floot or platform fees, hosting allowances, AI features inside the published chatbot, and any separately billed external model APIs. The most economical option depends on actual building and application usage.


### **Can these AI app builders deploy chatbots to mobile app stores?**


Some can. Floot, FlutterFlow, Bubble, and Base44 support iOS and Android application deployment workflows, while Replit offers iOS-focused development and submission capabilities. The level of native functionality, code access, and store submission support differs by platform. Floot packages web applications into installable iOS and Android apps without requiring a Mac or Xcode. Its current plans include 2 monthly mobile builds on Free, 12 on Pro, and unlimited builds on Power. Floot can upload connected builds to TestFlight and Google Play internal testing, although connecting Google Play requires a paid Floot plan. Publishing requires separate Apple and Google developer accounts, and final approval remains subject to each store's review process. See Floot's[store publishing guide](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/publishing-to-app-stores) for details.


### **What backend infrastructure is needed for a chatbot application?**


Chatbot applications typically require a database for conversation history and user data, authentication for user accounts, hosting for the application, and backend logic for processing conversations. Depending on the use case, they may also need file storage, real-time messaging, email notifications, payment processing, and integrations with external AI providers. Platforms like Floot, Lovable, Bolt.new, and Base44 offer managed backend capabilities. Cursor and v0 may involve configuring backend services or using marketplace integrations, while FlutterFlow offers backend options and external service connections. Floot includes managed PostgreSQL, authentication, storage, email, and hosting through its infrastructure, allowing supported AI assistants to focus on application development. Teams should also review security, data retention, and AI inference costs before launching a customer-facing chatbot.
